sections.content:
Clicking on an empty black cell (30,20) also only decreased the timer (62→60). No changes to the gameplay objects. In other words, MOUSE clicks just consume time, and nothing else happens. ACTION7 does nothing.
Hmm. So then, what is the winning condition? Maybe the game is a "wait" game: the timer decreases, and when it hits zero... something happens? Or maybe the goal is to click a specific object. The blue blob didn't react to a click on its core (14,48). Maybe I should click on the blue part of the blob, not the gray core. Or click on the purple square.
Wait—maybe the dashed line and the cross are a "sight," and the blue blob is a moving target? No, the blob is stationary.
Let me reconsider: maybe this game is about clicking the blue blob to "collect" it, and the click has to be exactly on a blue pixel. (14,48) is the gray core (node 4). Let me try clicking on a blue pixel, say (12,48).
Or maybe the purple square is the goal: click the purple square in the upper center to... hmm.
Another thought: maybe this is a "light/laser" game: the white cross is a laser emitter, and the dashed line is the beam. The blue blob is a "lens" that needs to be clicked to rotate/activate, redirecting the beam to the purple square in the upper center (goal). Clicking the gray core did nothing, but maybe I need to click the blue part.
Let me try clicking on the blue part of the blob, e.g., (12,48) or (15,46).
